verdict:
ESCALATE on FOUR standing mandatory triggers plus a FIFTH the record never saw. The escalation must land by 2026-08-21 - the FTC bench trial opens 2026-08-24, six trading days out.

(1) DISCORDANT BENCHES - red flat-to-quarter, blue half-starter. (2) ADVANCE OUTCOME - blue proposes seating a position. (3) BROKEN VERIFICATION SELF-REPORTED AT BOTH BENCHES - IBKR search_contracts permission-denied to red and to blue, so every price relationship in the record is arithmetic off a machine snapshot. (4) BINDING DATED BINARY at 2026-08-24 (FTC + state AGs v. Zillow/Redfin, EDVA, Judge Trenga, two-week bench trial).

(5) THE TRIGGER NEITHER BENCH SAW - CROSS-CLASS INCOHERENCE, AND IT IS THE HEADLINE. ZG is Zillow Group Class A. Z is Zillow Group Class C. Same CIK, same economics, same FTC trial, same CoStar tail, same 10-Q. The desk adjudicated Z on 2026-08-15: 'ESCALATION RULED: KILL entry-now... Remaining edge = an antitrust binary both benches concede is unpriceable - and size-cutting is NOT an instrument for unpriceability (doctrine: bounded business risk cuts size; unpriceable binaries gate). NO position into the 8/24 FTC trial; re-court POST-outcome.' Twenty-four hours later the ZG record reaches a half-starter into the same trial on the same facts. Both rulings cannot stand. Nothing in the ZG triage, red bench or blue bench mentions Z anywhere - the dispatch has no same-issuer / other-share-class lookup, so the desk came within one adjudication of seating a position in a name it had just killed.

AND THE CLASS ARITHMETIC MAKES ZG THE WRONG VEHICLE EVEN IF THE EXPOSURE WERE WANTED. Verified IBKR closes 2026-08-14: ZG $35.16 vs Z $34.78. ZG trades at a +1.09% PREMIUM to the economically identical non-voting C shares. If Zillow is ever seated it must be in the cheaper class at that moment - and the cheaper class today is the one already ruled KILL.

TAPE VERIFIED AT ADJUDICATION (IBKR works here; the denial was bench-side permission, not an outage). ZG daily closes: 8/05 36.89 (pre-print) | 8/06 33.76 | 8/07 33.95 | 8/10 34.07 | 8/11 34.27 | 8/12 33.49 | 8/13 36.23 | 8/14 35.16. Three results. (a) The pack's $35.16 is CONFIRMED as the 8/14 close - ZG's benches were anchored correctly, but by luck rather than by verification, since neither could check. (b) Red's drawdown anchors verify EXACTLY: 52-week high $90.22, low $29.03, so dd52 -61.0% and pct_off_low +21.1%, both as red stated - and low_13w = low_26w = low_52w = $29.03, meaning the 52-week low is FRESH, which supports red's 'knife, not base' reading rather than blue's. (c) Net through the print ZG is -4.7% (36.89 -> 35.16), the same modest-negative settled verdict the Z adjudication established at -3.7%. Note the 8/13 one-session +8.2% spike that contaminated the Z pack (33.49 -> 36.23 -> 35.16) is present in ZG too; it simply did not land in ZG's pack.

SUBSTANTIVE LEAN: KILL ENTRY-NOW, COHERING WITH Z.

BLUE WINS ITS CENTRAL CORRECTION AND IT MUST BE RECORDED. Red's headline kill - 'SBC ~15% of revenue, so EV/(adj EBITDA - SBC) is 40x+' - is itself the aggregation artifact red was chartered to hunt. Q2 SBC was $75M = 9.7% of $772M revenue; red used a stale 2022-era ratio. Corrected: EV ~$7.23B against an FY guide of $730-760M adj EBITDA less a ~$300M SBC run-rate is ~16x, and even red's own arithmetic never reaches 40x. GAAP was a $4M loss - breakeven, not floorless. Blue also found what red missed on the downside-bound question: $200M repurchased in Q2 with $1.1B of authorization remaining, about 14% of the cap. Red said nothing bounds the downside; something does.

BUT NONE OF THAT SURVIVES AS AN ENTRY CASE, FOR THREE REASONS THE RECORD ITSELF SUPPLIES. First, blue's own best new finding cuts against blue: adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDES 'FTC Matter litigation costs'. The marketed 26% margin - and therefore the ~16x - is struck on a number that capitalises the live binary out of its own denominator. Second, the CoStar tail is worse than red knew, and blue proved it: the motion to dismiss was DENIED on 2026-05-11, so red's own change-my-mind trigger ('CoStar MTD granted') was already dead when red wrote it; the count is 53,000 images and GREW post-complaint including republished removed images, which is a willfulness accelerant; the per-work statutory ceiling exceeds the market cap; and the 10-Q says verbatim that 'possible loss or range of loss is not estimable'. Worse, blue's 10-Q contingency extract shows FTC and Breidert but NO CoStar paragraph at all, flagged as possible proxy truncation and left UNVERIFIED. If CoStar is genuinely absent from the contingencies note while the plaintiff publicly floats >$1B, that is not a sizing input, it is a disclosure-integrity finding - and it is unclosed. Third and decisively: two unsized, not-estimable legal binaries, one opening in six trading days, is precisely the shape the Z ruling gated rather than sized. A half-starter is size-cutting applied to unpriceability, which the doctrine forbids.

WHAT SURVIVES FOR THE FILE ON THE BULL SIDE, STATED HONESTLY: the monetization refutation is real but much narrower than the triage claimed. Red's decomposition, CONFIRMED by blue, shows Residential - the funnel-exposed segment the disintermediation thesis actually attacks - at +7% revenue, roughly +9% per unique user, not the marketed +20%. The blend is carried by Rentals +31% and Mortgages +75%. Blue's rebuttal that this is mix rather than artifact is fair - property managers and purchase originations do not grow like that through a collapsing funnel - but it relocates the growth into the segment that is ON TRIAL (Rentals is 42% of incremental growth), which is the opposite of a hedge. Also unadjudicated: 10 Form 144s filed 8/11-8/14 into the pre-trial window, 10b5-1 status UNVERIFIED by either bench. || SESSION RULING: ESCALATION RULED: KILL entry-now, COHERENT WITH Z (same CIK, same trial, same 10-Q — ZG is Class A, Z is Class C). The 8/15 Z ruling governs both: an antitrust binary both benches concede is unpriceable GATES, it does not size-cut. ZG's +1.09% premium to the economically identical killed class is itself the tell — no discount for identical exposure. NO position into the 8/24 FTC trial; re-court POST-outcome, both classes together, cheaper class preferred if re-entered. cross_share_class_ruling_coherence guard harvested — the desk came one adjudication from buying the expensive class of a name it killed 24 hours earlier.
